standard.title: Deliver structured presentations
standard.description: create and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations on personal and learnt topics, which include an opening, middle and concluding statement; some topic-specific vocabulary and appropriate gesture, volume and pace
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and deliver short spoken texts to report ideas and events to peers (AC9EFLY07). They have not yet structured presentations with explicit opening, middle and concluding statements, or deliberately used topic-specific vocabulary and paralinguistic features (gesture, volume, pace) as presenting tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations with an opening, middle and concluding statement, topic vocabulary, and appropriate gesture, volume and pace.

nodes.label: Structuring a presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can organise a short presentation with an identifiable opening, middle and concluding statement.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan and deliver a short presentation that has a beginning, a middle with at least one key idea, and a conclusion.
nodes.typical_width: Create and deliver presentations with a clear opening (introducing the topic), a structured middle (key information or ideas) and a concluding statement (summarising or closing).
wider: Experiment with different types of opening — a question, a statement, a surprising fact — and discuss which works best for the topic
Compare presentations with and without a clear structure and discuss the difference for the audience
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a planned three-part structure, students cannot deploy topic vocabulary or paralinguistic features purposefully in N2 and N3 — unstructured delivery makes both vocabulary placement and gesture/pace meaningless.

response_modes.reason: Planning a three-part structure requires students to make deliberate sequencing decisions — what goes first, what is the main content, how do I end? A simple planning scaffold (opening / key ideas / conclusion) supports this reasoning before the performance.

success_criteria: Student's presentation has an identifiable opening that introduces the topic
Student's presentation has a concluding statement that closes or summarises

nodes.label: Topic vocabulary in presentations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use topic-specific vocabulary in their presentations to communicate precisely about the topic.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two topic-specific words correctly in an oral presentation.
nodes.typical_width: Incorporate topic-specific vocabulary appropriate to the subject matter across the presentation, using words that communicate precisely about the topic.
wider: Explain an unfamiliar topic-specific word to the audience as part of the presentation
Compare presentations with and without topic vocabulary — discuss how precision changes the listener's understanding
success_criteria: Student uses at least two topic-specific words correctly in their presentation
Student's vocabulary choice is appropriate to the topic

nodes.label: Gesture, volume and pace
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use appropriate gesture, volume and pace when delivering a presentation to support meaning and engage the audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a presentation at an audible volume, at a pace that allows the audience to follow, and with at least one deliberate gesture.
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate volume (loud enough for the audience), pace (neither too fast nor too slow for the purpose), and gesture (to emphasise or demonstrate) when delivering presentations, varying these for effect.
wider: Experiment with volume and pace for different purposes — retelling a scary moment versus explaining how to make something
Record a presentation and review the use of gesture, volume and pace — identify one area to improve

response_modes.reason: Managing gesture, volume and pace simultaneously with content delivery requires repeated practice. Students need multiple presentation opportunities before paralinguistic features are used consistently and deliberately.

success_criteria: Student speaks at an audible volume throughout the presentation
Student uses at least one deliberate gesture to support meaning
